notes.title: Desktop Life
notes.summary: MediaDesk now behaves like a proper desktop app: it can start with Windows, live in the tray, switch to light mode, and has a Settings page for all of it.

items.title: Settings page
items.text: Sidebar → Settings holds everything about how MediaDesk starts, looks and updates on this PC.

items.title: Run when Windows starts
items.text: Turn it on in Settings and MediaDesk opens by itself after you sign in to Windows.
details: "Start minimized to the tray" makes it start quietly in the tray instead of opening a window.
Off by default. It only works in the installed app.

items.title: Hide to tray
items.text: With "Hide to the tray when minimized" on, minimizing tucks MediaDesk into the tray next to the clock. Click the tray icon to bring it back.

items.title: Tray shortcuts
items.text: Right-click the tray icon to jump straight to Dashboard, Clients, New client, Pipeline or Media library, check for updates, open Settings, or quit.
details: When an update is waiting, the tray menu shows "Update to V…".

items.title: Light mode
items.text: Choose Dark, Light or Match Windows in Settings → Appearance. Match Windows follows your Windows setting live, even while MediaDesk is open.

items.title: Update schedule
items.text: Turn automatic update checks on or off, and pick how often: every 15 minutes, 30 minutes, hour, 3 hours, or only at startup.

items.title: App icon
items.text: MediaDesk has its own icon in the window and the tray (a placeholder until the final logo is chosen).

items.title: Data folder
items.text: Settings shows where your data lives on this PC, with a button to open it.
The desktop shortcut and Start menu icon change with the next full installer. Updates can only change the icon inside the app and the tray.
Closing the window with × still quits MediaDesk. Only minimizing hides it to the tray.
